# Past-Paper Practice

## When to use

Exam preparation method: solving real past papers under timed conditions and marking them against the official scheme. Use when a learner is preparing for a board, entrance, or university exam.

## Steps

1. Get the official past papers and mark schemes for the exam (from the examining body or the school).
2. Sit one paper under timed conditions with no notes. Keep to the time for each section.
3. Mark it with the official scheme. Use a different colour for marks lost.
4. For each mark lost, write the cause (knowledge, method, reading the question, time) and the fix.

## Example

A learner does a two-hour physics paper in 2 hours 10 minutes, marks it, and finds 12 marks lost on units and 8 on timing. The plan for next week addresses both.

## Common mistakes

- Looking up answers during the attempt
- Marking vaguely ('mostly right') instead of against the scheme
- Doing only the paper you like, instead of the whole range of question types

## Coach rules

- Explain the method briefly, then have the learner try it on their own material straight away.
- Check at the end of the session: did the learner actually do the method, or only talk about it?
